analysis.summary: The PR introduces logic errors in the discount display calculation and layout alignment that will cause broken UI text and misaligned comparison columns.

bugs.title: Broken string replacement logic in discount tag trimming
bugs.description: The logic to trim long discount tags is flawed. It creates `staticText` by removing the placeholder from the template, then tries to find that exact `staticText` inside a string where the placeholder has been replaced by a dynamic value. This search will fail if there is any text following the placeholder (or if removal left double spaces), rendering the trimming logic non-functional.
bugs.risk: UI labels that are too long will not be truncated as intended, causing the discount badge (Tag) to overflow or break the layout in the comparison grid.

bugs.title: Incorrect vertical alignment calculation
bugs.description: The vertical alignment logic calculates the `maxHeight` of all price boxes but then sets the `minHeight` to `maxHeight - 5`. This prevents elements from actually aligning correctly as they will be 5px shorter than the tallest element, defeating the purpose of the height-syncing logic.
bugs.risk: Incorrect horizontal alignment across comparison columns, making price and discount information appear staggered and unprofessional.

bugs.title: Potential 'undefined' string injection in discount UI
bugs.description: The `dynamicValue` calculation for the discount tag does not provide a safe fallback for the entire string construction. If `promoBadgePrice` properties are missing (which occurs when `hasPromoBadgePrice` is true for the row but false for a specific product), the template literal will evaluate to `"-undefined%"` or `"undefined"` and display it to the user.
bugs.risk: End-users will see broken 'undefined' text inside promotional badges on products that do not have active discounts but are part of a comparison row where other products do.

notBugs.reason: Applying the discount layout to all products in a row (even non-discounted ones) when at least one has a discount is a common pattern to ensure column alignment in comparison features.
The property rename appears to be consistently applied across the types and the primary component logic provided in the diff.
